subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve near-`maxChars` paragraph boundaries with explicit seam metadata, a reserve-width split, or an intentionally partial text-only repair?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and this PR improves the common path, but the remaining edge case needs a maintainer choice about whether to widen the delivery contract or accept a documented partial repair.

options.title: Require complete boundary preservation
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit seam metadata
options.body: Carry paragraph/newline/hard-split boundary semantics through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if text-only chunks cannot satisfy the invariants.

options.title: Accept the partial text repair
options.body: Maintainers may knowingly land the common-case improvement while leaving the near-limit boundary tracked on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require complete boundary preservation
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest available history across block-reply coalescing, chunking hardening, and current-file layout for the affected surfaces.
